en: One fascicle of the *Vajraśekhara-sūtra Tārā-bodhisattva Recitation Method*.
Compiled by the Grand Master of the Household, Peer of the State, Special Advancement, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Sushan.
I take refuge in the Sovereign King of Yoga, who dwells securely in the illusion-like samādhi;
Who, throughout the entire ocean of pure and defiled realms, Is able to manifest various bodies according to the types of beings.
Relying upon the gateway of the Lotus Union, I reveal the Dharma of Tārā’s Great Compassion.
To cause those who practice samādhi to leave behind the two vehicles,
to swiftly perfect the perfection of supernatural powers through compassionless concentration, and to be able to suddenly realize the stage of the Tathāgata—
the practitioner should give rise to the mind of Samantabhadra and receive the Vajra precepts in full from a teacher.
Disregarding one’s own body and life, one should give rise to a mind of loving-kindness; only then can one endure entry into the wheel of liberation.
One should receive the samaya from the master, including the mudrās and secret mantras as explained in the sūtras.
One should regard the ācārya with the same reverence as for a Buddha, and maintain a heart of earnest devotion toward one's fellow practitioners.
Whether in mountain retreats or forest hermitages, by flowing springs, bathing pools,
or delightful places; at mountain peaks, stone caves, or beside solitary trees— there one should establish a mandala according to the ritual rules,
adorn a sacred chamber, install the primary deity, and dwell with single-minded devotion while making offerings according to one's means.
Universally observing the oceans of Buddhas in the ten directions, perform confession and make vows exactly as taught.

To accomplish the vajra-nature of the three karmas, one should visualize the syllable *HŪṂ* within the two hands, the tongue, and the heart, forming five-pronged vajras of the five wisdoms. Through this empowerment, one will attain all *siddhis*.
Next, one should form the mudrā called Awakening: with both hands forming vajra-fists, hook the *tarjanī* and *madhyamā* fingers together and extend the *anāmikā* and *kaniṣṭhā* fingers;
with the two middle fingers touching, this is named the Arising Seal (*utthāna-mudrā*).
The mantra is as follows:
Next, one should pay homage to the Honored One Akṣobhya, seeking the stage of non-retrogression by offering up one's body.
Joining the vajra-palms and extending them above the crown of the head, with the whole body prostrated to the ground, the mantra for this mental prostration is as follows:
Next, prostrate to the Honored One Ratnasambhava of the South. With body surrendered, supplicate for the stage of empowerment.
Joining the vajra-palms at the heart, touch the forehead to the ground and pay homage with sincere devotion.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, prostrate to the Honored One, Lord Avalokiteśvara. To request the samādhi, offer up your body;
join your palms like a vajra at the crown of your head and, placing your mouth to the ground, reverently recite the mantra as follows:
Next, prostrate to the Honored One Amoghasiddhi; with palms joined at the heart in the gesture of the Vajra of Skillful Wisdom, and bowing the head to the ground,
he makes this request with the mantra:
Next, visualize all Buddhas pervading the void; one should perform the *dhāraṇī-mudrā* and universally prostrate at their feet.
With the left hand and right hand crossed back-to-back (*jñāna-vajra*), place the right knee on the ground and rest [the hands] upon the crown of the head.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, with the mantra of sublime accomplishment, universally wishing that all sentient beings may attain *siddhi*,
and in accordance with the dharma praised by all Tathāgatas, one should pray for empowerment and swift accomplishment.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, one should sit with legs crossed and the body upright, purifying the three karmas so that they are completely clean.
Since the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure, may oneself and others be rendered entirely stainless.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, perform the Lotus Samaya-bond: interlace the ten fingers into a firm bind, and extend the *kṣānti* (ring) and *praṇidhi* (little finger) fingers together like lotus petals.
Visualize one’s own body as identical to that of the Honored One Tārā.
The mantra is as follows: [Mantra]
Next, bind the mudrā of the Samādhi of Supreme Joy: Firmly interlock the two hands of concentration and wisdom;
join the fingers of patience and aspiration at their centers; and extend the fingers of generosity, wisdom, meditation, and knowledge so they touch one another.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, one should open the heart and enter the Buddha-wisdom. Second, perform the empowerment of the two breasts with the *tāḍa* mudrā;
form the *vajrabandha* at the front of the heart. Third, pull it open like a door opening;
the mantra is as follows:
Next, contemplate the syllable A at the lotus pedestal, adorned with two dots, forming the meditative wisdom of quiescence;
bend the fingers into the vajra-bond and summon the syllable to flow into the heart.
The mantra is as follows: [OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ].
Next, bind the Secret Vajra Fist; by means of this empowerment, make it firm.
Enter the mudrā with the *jñāna* and *vajra* fingers placed in the position of progress and power (*vīrya*). Thus, one can maintain [the vow] firmly without falling back.
The true words say:
Next, bind the Lotus Mudrā for Subduing Māras; by this, purify all obstacles and difficulties.
One should employ the ritual of the Vajra-Pañjali: extend the *tarjanī* fingers like tusks, with the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers held inward;
manifesting a wrathful countenance out of a heart of compassion, rotate three times to the right to establish the boundaries of the directions.
The mantra is as follows:

Next, one should straighten the body and abide in samādhi; with the two hands crossed to form the seal of concentration, the dust of the realm of space is the ocean of all Buddhas. One should awaken [the mind] to contemplate the true heart.
The mantra is as follows:
One should visualize the letter A as a lunar disc, and further clarify it by means of the mantra.
The mantra is: [Mantra].
Because the intrinsic nature of one’s own mind is pure, one should skillfully contemplate the mantra of the Vajra Lotus:
"In order to accomplish the single characteristic of purity, may it gradually blossom in accordance with the Dharmadhātu."
One immediately attains the Great Compassion Samādhi, which is able to universally purify the realms of sentient beings.
The mantra is as follows:
In order to bring this samādhi to full maturity, one gains mastery over extending and contracting [all things] at will.
Gradually withdrawing the lotus of wisdom, one measures it against one's own body; then, universally emitting pure light, the mantra of samādhi is recited:
Next, by means of the firm and wondrous mantra, one empowers [the body] so that it cannot be shaken.
The mantra says:
All Tathāgatas manifested within the expanse of space Enter entirely into the Flower of Awakening as a single essence;
One should know them to be equal to all Buddhas, The embodiment of the firm vow for Bodhi.
The mantra says:
One should visualize the wondrous lotus as the Honored One (Bhagavatī). Her body is pure and full, the color of emerald-gold;
she wears a necklace of exquisite mani jewels and bears Amitāyus upon her jeweled crown.
The right hand displays the mudrā of granting supreme boons;
the left, in the gesture of meditative concentration, holds a blue lotus while abiding within the lunar disc at the heart.
Radiating the light of universal compassion throughout the three realms, one next performs the empowerment by means of the root blue lotus mudrā, pervading the heart, forehead, throat, and crown.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the Jewel Seal (Ratnamudrā) for self-consecration.
With both hands firmly forming the Vajrabandha, the thumbs and ring fingers are joined like a jewel; perform the empowerment at the forehead and tie it behind the head.
The mantra is as follows:
Having formed the two hands like hanging garlands, one should then don the firm armor;
forming the vajra-fist, extend the forefinger and middle finger while visualizing the two syllables Oṃ and Chin on their tips.
At the heart, back, navel, waist, and both knees, as well as the throat, forehead, and crown of the head, one should circle [the hands] three times;
before the *dāna* and *prajñā* [fingers], the celestial robes are spread and hang down. This will enable one to become firm and unwavering.
One should strike with the two palms three times; this is called the ritual of the Lotus Joy Seal (*padma-harṣa-mudrā*).
The mantra says:

Next, one should adorn and purify the Buddha-fields; desiring to serve all Tathāgatas, one should clearly contemplate the inexhaustible ocean of fragrant water, wherein the wondrous lotus supports the Flower Treasury World-realm.
The maṇi-jewel palaces are magnificently adorned, surpassing all the wondrous offerings of the devas;

the devas of the void constitute the fifth [assembly]. May whatever they desire arise from the void, and with hearts joyful in making offerings to the assembly of noble ones, may their wishes be universally fulfilled according to their intent.
Having empowered [the site] with this truth, one should perform the ritual of the vajra-joined palms (*vajra-añjali*) and recite the mantra:
"Upon a jeweled ground adorned with a flower seat, by means of the *dharmadhātu* syllable *Dhuṃ*, may the principal deity be accomplished."
Emitting pure light that surpasses the sun and moon, surrounded on all sides by a retinue of lotuses;
next, through the secret expedient of invocation, summon the body of the Honored One into the essence of wisdom.
Firmly binding the two hands of concentration and wisdom, bend the fingers of the "advancement" and "power" positions outward like hooks.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the Great Seal of the Lotus Lasso. With the palms joined like lotuses, the wisdom fingers enter into the *jñāna-muṣṭi* (wisdom-fist) mudrā.
By means of this secret seal and mantra, one may summon and cause the entry of the *iṣṭadevatā* (chosen deity).
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the lotus hands into the *śṛṅkhalā-mudrā* (chain seal). Hook the thumbs, index fingers, and wisdom fingers together;
by binding them thus with this lotus-stopping seal, one can cause the *iṣṭadevatā* (honored deity) to remain steadfastly present.
The mantra is as follows.
Next, bind the Lotus Bell Secret Seal: bend the wisdom fingers (the ring and little fingers) into the lotus-palms.
By means of this secret seal and mantra, one is able to cause the Honored One to experience sublime joy.
The mantra is as follows:

Next, with pleasing and sublime verses, holding aloft the argha vessel, one offers fragrant water whose wondrous sound pervades the boundless realms; through this empowerment, swift accomplishment is attained.
The mantra is as follows:

Next, one should extensively arrange the four inner offerings. With the palms joined and the fingers extended upward, establishing the dhyāna and prajñā mudrās, one plays with this lotus; thereby, one is able to fulfill the dāna-pāramitā.
The mantra is as follows.
Next, bind the secret mudrā of the lotus garland: by extending the arms forward with the palms joined like a lotus, one makes an offering of a flower garland;
thereby, one shall fulfill the perfection of pure ethical discipline.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, form the Lotus Song-Singing Mudrā. With palms joined like a lotus, extend them from the navel to the mouth and scatter [the flowers] as an offering;
this is the sublime Dharma-sound of this Tathāgata, which can fulfill the perfection of patience (kṣānti-pāramitā).
The mantra is as follows:
Next, perform the Lotus Dance Offering. By whirling the lotus-hand dance and placing it upon the crown of the head through this mudrā and mantra, one swiftly perfects the pāramitā of diligence.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the Lotus Incense-offering Mudrā. With palms joined like a lotus, scatter the incense as if burning it.
By the power of this Brahma-incense mudrā, one shall realize the perfection of meditative concentration (dhyāna-pāramitā).
The mantra is as follows:

Next, perform the lotus-flower offering. By scattering flowers from the palms of the lotus hands as if making an offering, and because of the adornment of these sublime flowers, one swiftly realizes the Prajñāpāramitā.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the mudrā of the Lotus Lamp. By pressing the fingers of wisdom (jñāna) and meditation (dhyāna) against the lotus-hand, one makes this offering of light;
thereby, one shall fulfill the pāramitā of skillful means (upāya).
The mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the mudrā of the Lotus Unguent. Spread the palms over the heart like applying unguent;
by means of this mantra and the ritual of the mudrā, one can fulfill the perfection of the vow.
The mantra is as follows.

Next, bind the fundamental mudrā of the Honzon: with this mudrā, empower the heart center by placing the two *jñānamuṣṭi* (wisdom fists) with their joints facing away from each other, and joining the *tarjanī* (forefinger), *madhyamā* (middle finger), *anāmikā* (ring finger), and *kaniṣṭhā* (pinky) fingers together.
The mantra is as follows.

Next, bind the heart-mudrā of Amoghatārā. Empower the forehead with this mudrā according to the characteristics of the previously mentioned fundamental secret mudrā, with the exception that the thumbs and wisdom-fingers (middle fingers) are raised and made to touch one another.
The mantra is as follows.
Next, form the mudrā of the Honzon’s jeweled crown: place this great mudrā upon the crown of the head;

as with the previous heart-mudrā, extend the *kṣānti* (ring) and *praṇidhi* (little finger), while the two fingers of the *vajra* (forefinger) and *bala* (middle finger) are bent back at their joints.
The mantra is as follows.
Next, bind the seal of true empowerment (*bhūtādhiṣṭhāna-mudrā*). By means of this, one can summon all [deities];
it is like the previous crown-jewel empowerment seal (*abhiṣeka-ratnamakuṭa-mudrā*), with the sole difference that one proceeds and returns using the seal of diligence (*vīryapāramitā*).
The mantra is as follows.
Next, form the seal for destroying all māras: by means of this, one can subdue those who are difficult to tame.
Following the previous method for the consecration crown seal, extend the fingers of strength straight and rotate them to the right.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, one should array the syllable-gates upon one’s own body: the syllable *Oṃ* on the crown of the head;
*Ta* on the forehead; *Ra* on the two eyes; *Dhu* on the two shoulders; *Da* at the heart; and *Ra* at the navel.
With the syllable *Ṭha*, the two knees; with *Ḍha*, the two shins; with *Sva-ja-ha*, the four-faced Lord enters one’s own body.
Through this empowerment, becoming non-dual in essence, one should form the fundamental mudrā of the blue lotus and recite the hundred-syllable mantra of the Lotus.
The two wings of concentration and wisdom are crossed within; the thumbs and ring fingers are held upright against one another.
The mantra is: Having recited the hundred-syllable mantra, without releasing the previous mudrā, one should contemplate the root vidyā.
The mantra is as follows:
Furthermore, having empowered the rosary with the mantra, one should hold it upon the crown of the head and recite the mantra at the heart.
The mantra is as follows:
When the prescribed number of recitations has been completed, again offer arghya water and chant sublime praises.
Having once more presented the eight offerings and made aspirations, dissolve the visualization of the boundary and return the Honored One to his original palace.
Re-forming the previous lotus-samaya seal, scatter flowers upon one’s crown and prostrate at his feet.
The mantra is as follows:
Having offered farewell to all the deities, perform the empowerment, don the armor, and remain firmly established in the samādhi of the deity; then dwell at ease, whether sitting or walking.
Furthermore, one should recite the Mahāyāna scriptures, constantly maintaining pure karma without interruption;
thus one shall obtain the direct manifestation of Tārā before one’s eyes, and all sought-after supreme vows shall be fulfilled.
In this present life, one shall enter the Stage of Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*), and after sixteen births, one shall attain *bodhi*.
One fascicle of the *Vajraśekhara-sūtra: The Recitation Method of Bodhisattva Tārā*
